label: text
text: The thresholding logic used by a perceptron is very harsh !

label: text
text: For example, let us return to our problem of deciding whether we will like or dislike a movie

label: text
text: Consider that we base our decision only on one input x 1 = criticsRating ∈ (0, 1)

label: text
text: If the threshold is 0.5 and (-w 0 = 0.5) ( w 1 = 1)

label: text
text: What about a movie with criticsRating = 0.49 ? (dislike)

label: text
text: then what would be the decision for a movie with criticsRating = 0.51 ? (like)

label: text
text: It seems harsh that we would like a movie with rating 0.51 but not one with a rating of 0.49

label: picture
text: Figure 6

label: text
text: This behavior is not a characteristic of the specific problem we chose or the specific weight and threshold that we chose

label: text
text: It is a characteristic of the perceptron function itself which behaves like a step function

label: text
text: There will always be this sudden change in the decision (from 0 to 1) when crosses the threshold w x i =1 ∑ n i i -w 0

label: text
text: For most real world applications we would expect a smoother decision function which gradually changes from 0 to 1

label: picture
text: Figure 7

label: text
text: Introducing sigmoid neurons where the output function is much smoother than the step function

label: text
text: Here is one form of the sigmoid function called the logistic function

label: text
text: We no longer see a sharp transition around the threshold -w 0

label: text
text: Also the output is no longer binary but a real value between 0 and 1 which can be interpreted as a probability. y

label: text
text: Instead of a like/dislike decision we get the probability of liking the movie.

label: text
